question.text: Scenario: Meena Sharma, a 55-year-old retired school teacher from Jaipur, has mutual fund investments across 3 schemes of PQR Mutual Fund. She visits the Investor Service Centre (ISC) with the following requests: Request 1: She has recently moved from Jaipur to Udaipur and wants to update her address. She carries her new Aadhaar card showing the Udaipur address. Request 2: She has opened a new bank account with a different bank (Bank of Rajasthan) and wants all future redemption proceeds and IDCW payouts to go to this new account. She carries a cancelled cheque of the new account and her old bank's passbook. Request 3: She wants to add her daughter (Priya, age 28) and son (Rahul, age 32) as nominees with 60% and 40% allocation respectively. Currently, no nominee is registered. Request 4: She has not received her CAS for the last 6 months and wants to understand why and get it reissued. Request 5: She wants to know if she can consolidate her 3 folios — Folio 1 is in her single name, Folio 2 is joint with her husband (Meena + Suresh), and Folio 3 is in her single name with a different bank account. Question 1 of 5: For Request 1 (address change), what is the correct way to process it?

answer.text: Only a verbal request since she's visiting the ISC in person
A signed letter requesting the change; no document proof needed for existing KYC-compliant investors

If her folio is KRA-compliant, she must submit a KRA KYC update form with PAN, the new address and Aadhaar (or other documentary address proof); for non-KYC folios, she submits self-attested PAN and address proof at the AMC/RTA ISC
She must complete fresh KYC since her address has changed

explanation.text: The Logic: Address change processing depends on KYC status. For a KRA-compliant folio, the fund will not register the address change directly — the investor must update the address through KRA using a KYC update form along with PAN, the new address and documentary address proof such as Aadhaar. For a non-KYC folio, the investor submits self-attested PAN and address proof at the AMC/RTA ISC. Either way, this is an update, not a fresh KYC. The Trap: A verbal request or a signed letter without proof is not sufficient, and a fresh KYC is not required. The most common miss is treating the AMC/RTA ISC as the correct destination even for KRA-compliant folios — the KRA route is mandatory in that case. Note: Source: NISM Series II-B (RTA Mutual Fund) workbook — KRA route for address changes on KRA-compliant folios; AMC/RTA ISC route for non-KYC folios.
